_comment: Retrieval telemetry behind results/musique_pareto_acc.json, same runs and same 128 queries.
WITHIN a model, as the corpus grows: doc_hit_rate (is the gold document's slot in the top-k at
all?) stays high while mem_pos_weight_mass (fraction of softmax mass over retrieved slots that
lands on the gold document) collapses. The model keeps FINDING the gold document and
progressively stops ATTENDING to it. That much is solid.
ACROSS models it does NOT transfer, and an earlier version of this file claimed it did.
ground4layer at c8192 has mem_pos_weight_mass 0.0275 -- far BELOW hard-neg's 0.113 at the same
corpus -- yet scores 0.281 vs 0.211. With 4 layers x top-k 128 and ~54 effective slots it
gathers enough total evidence despite thin per-slot mass. Low weight-mass therefore does not by
itself predict low accuracy; it is a within-model diagnostic, not a cross-architecture one.
The two memory architectures do not order consistently either: ground4layer minus hard-neg is
mixed result, not evidence that more memory layers help or hurt.
_noise_floor: RAG c512 repeat: 0.3984 vs 0.3906 -> ~0.008 on n=128. Differences below ~0.02 are not resolvable. The c8192 RAG-vs-ground4layer gap (+0.0078) is AT this floor and is a tie, not a win.
